_about: Raw JSON-RPC between the host (agent.py via mcp_host.py) and the claims-system server, captured by wiretap.py on the run in runs/trace_wire.log (CLM-2024-10004). 'message' is each line exactly as it crossed stdio, parsed; the byte-exact lines are runs/wire_raw.jsonl lines 1-7. Lines 8-9 (tools/call get_adjuster_notes, id 4) have the same shape and are not repeated here. 't_s' is seconds since the wiretap started.
where_the_model_call_happens: The model is called only in the host - agent.py run() -> llm.chat -> Groq - in the 0.786 s gap between the tools/list reply (t=0.807) and tools/call id 3 (t=1.593) when nothing crosses this wire; it never happens on the wire or inside either server, where tools/call is plain Python reading claims.json.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag, always "2.0". Present on every message in both directions.
annotations.id: 1 - request id picked by the host. The reply must carry the same id; that is the only thing pairing a reply with its request.
annotations.method: "initialize" - must be the first message of the session. The server answers nothing else before it.
annotations.params.protocolVersion: "2025-11-25" - the MCP revision the host speaks. The server replies with the one it will use.
annotations.params.capabilities: {} - the host offers the server nothing back: no sampling (the server cannot ask our model for a completion), no roots, no elicitation. A server that wanted to run our model would need sampling here, and it is not granted.
annotations.params.clientInfo: "mcp" 0.1.0 - the SDK default; the host never named itself. Informational only - it is not authentication.

annotations.result: Present means success. A failed request would carry "error" instead, never both.
annotations.result.capabilities: tools.listChanged=false: the tool list is fixed for the session, so the single tools/list the host makes at start-up is complete. prompts and resources are declared too, but the server lists none - declared is not offered.
annotations.result.protocolVersion: "2025-11-25" - agreed; both sides now speak this revision.
annotations.result.serverInfo: name "claims-system", version "" - the server reports no version, so we cannot tell which build we are running. Carried into risk_note.md.

annotations.method: "notifications/initialized" - the host says the handshake is done. No id, so it is a notification: no reply is sent or expected.
"tools/list" - discovery. No params, so no pagination cursor: first page. This reply is the only source of the tool list the model sees - mcp_host.py turns it into the Groq tools parameter unchanged.

tools.description: Current status and policy facts for one claim, by claim number (CLM-YYYY-nnnnn): status, policy number, policy line, endorsement forms attached, Coverage A limit, excess, date of loss, first notice of loss and claimed amount. Does not return the adjuster's notes - use get_adjuster_notes for those.
tools.name: get_claim_status

tools.description: The adjuster's dated file notes for one claim, by claim number (CLM-YYYY-nnnnn), oldest first. An empty list means no notes have been written yet.
tools.name: get_adjuster_notes

annotations.result: One page; no nextCursor, so the list is complete.
annotations.result.tools: 2 tools: get_claim_status, get_adjuster_notes. For each: name (what the model will call), description (the server author's docstring - goes verbatim into our model's prompt, so a third party writes part of our prompt), inputSchema (JSON Schema, passed to the model as the tool's parameters). claim_number has no pattern in the schema; the CLM-YYYY-nnnnn format is only stated in prose.

annotations.params: Written by the model, not the host:
annotations.params.name: "get_claim_status" - chosen by the model on lap 1. The host only looked up which server listed this name and forwarded the call.
annotations.params.arguments: {"claim_number": "CLM-2024-10004"} - written by the model; the server validates it against inputSchema before running.

annotations.result: A tool result - a JSON-RPC success even when the tool fails:
annotations.result.content: One text block holding the claim record as JSON text. This string is what the host hands the model as the tool message. Adjuster notes are not in it - a separate tool.
annotations.result.isError: false - tool-level success. A tool failure (e.g. claim not found) comes back as isError=true inside a normal result, not as a JSON-RPC error, so the model gets to read the message and recover.
